The jungle look is so pretty with Discus!

How hard are they to take care of? I've only heard here and there that they're kind-of a pain in the tooshie!

I've had the tank up and running about 8 months now. I just added the discus in the last week. Someone locally had to move and needed to re-home them. I've wanted discus for a while, but I'd always had fish that liked water temps that were too cold to get along well with the discus. This tank I tried to buy fish that were more heat tolerant, and I'm doing more water changes than I typically would. So far they have voracious appetites, and seem to be loving the tank. I'll be adding a few more in the next week from another local buyer who needs to find new homes for their discus.

I did get special food for them, but check back in a few months and I'll let you know.

I'm trying to keep nitrates below 20ppm at all times, which in a 125G tank means some real water changes. The nice part is I use the water from the 125G to do water changes in my 30G, which I then use the water from there to water the office plants.

So they pretty much need fairly clean water like any other fish would? And perhaps a more special diet, I'm sure! My husband mentioned he'd like Discus/Angels but Discus were kind-of off the board since "they're super up-tight" as far as water parameters go, but yours look really nice!

If it comes down to it we'll just have to do more and more research, the Discus kind of freak me out but their colors are very unique!

Look forward to seeing more of your fish though! :)

12 slices Turkey bacon, cut into 1/2 inch pieces 1 medium potato, cut into small cubes 2 green onions, thinly sliced 1/2 tsp. chili powder 1 carton 8 oz. frozen, thawed or refrigerated cholesterol-free egg product, beaten

Directions

  1. Place turkey bacon and potato in non-stick skillet.
  2. Cook on medium heat 12 minutes or until potatoes are fork-tender, stirring frequently.
  3. Stir in onions and chili powder.
  4. Pour egg product evenly over mixture;
